learning_outcomes.text: Utilize the basic properties of real and complex numbers and perform fundamental operations with them.
Use the basic elements of Linear Algebra: systems of linear equations, vector spaces and linear applications and use matrices to simplify their study.
Identify metric properties in vector spaces, through the scalar product, norm or distance.
Calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors and diagonalize endomorphisms and matrices.
Solve geometric problems in the plane and in space.
Identify the basic elements of differential equations and systems of differential equations and use algebraic tools to solve elementary cases.

syllabus_topics: Theme 2. Systems of linear equations and matrices.
2.2. Solving systems using Gauss's Method. Application to the calculation of the inverse matrix.
3.2. Linear combinations and linear independence. Bases and dimension. Coordinates.
4.3. Kernel and image of an application. Classification of linear applications.
5.3. Applications to the solution of systems of linear differential equations.
6.1. Euclidean vector space. Scalar product and metric properties.
2. Matrix calculation and systems of equations
3. Vector spaces and changes of basis
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) for the subject is calculated as NF = 0.15*NL + maximum (0.15*NA + 0.7*NC, 0.85*NC), where NL is the laboratory practice grade, NA is the classroom practice grade, and NC is the average grade of the written controls. To pass the subject, a minimum of 2.5 out of 10 points must be obtained in each of the two partial controls. If this minimum is not reached in any of them, the final grade will be a fail, and the numerical grade in the transcript will be the minimum between NF and 4.5. For extraordinary calls, a written exam with two parts and a laboratory practical test will be conducted, using the same grading formula.
